asset.title: From Governed Knowledge to an Auditable Institutional Asset
asset.dek: A reference workflow for policy-aware, AI-assisted publishing with explicit human authorization.
body: Institutional publishing requires more than content generation. It requires traceable source material, applicable policies, specialist review, explicit authorization, and durable evidence of every decision.

The BBA Publisher Reference Demo models that lifecycle as a Mission. The Mission retrieves relevant policies, classifies the source, prepares an editorial brief, produces a draft Institutional Asset, and records review findings before a human can approve or reject release.

The browser demo intentionally replays a deterministic reference package. This keeps the build transparent and reproducible while allowing policy retrieval, workflow transitions, review handling, human authorization, and audit logging to execute locally.
The result is not a production publishing platform. It is an executable reference implementation showing how governed knowledge can become an auditable institutional asset.

medium.title: From One Governed Asset to Channel-Specific Publishing
medium.summary: Why a governed Institutional Asset needs editorial adaptation before distribution.
medium.body:
## A governed source needs a governed path

Institutional publishing is more than producing a single text. A source note is retrieved against relevant policy, shaped into an Institutional Asset, reviewed for claims, and held for explicit human authorization.

## Why adaptation matters

The approved asset is the source of truth, but each channel has a different audience and reading convention. A long-form editorial channel can provide context and sections; a short social channel needs a clear hook; a technical community needs implementation detail. The message remains traceable while the presentation changes.

## What this reference demonstrates

The BBA Publisher Reference Demo creates deterministic channel variants from one approved asset. Every variant keeps the Mission and parent asset references, runs a channel-specific review, and requires its own human decision.

**Disclosure:** synthetic data, deterministic output, and no external publishing. Read the reference workflow and inspect its audit trail.

dev-community.title: Building a Deterministic, Governed Publishing Workflow
dev-community.summary: Implementation notes for adapting one reviewed asset to multiple channels.
dev-community.body:
## What this demonstrates

This reference implementation turns governed knowledge into a reviewed Institutional Asset and then derives channel-specific variants. The core flow is: policy retrieval, mission planning, deterministic production, claims review, and human authorization.

### Implementation notes

- Channel Profiles are local JSON data, not hard-coded UI rules.
- Each variant preserves `missionId` and `parentAssetId`.
- A deterministic review checks claims, disclosure, titles, tags, Markdown, call to action, and length.
- A rejected variant does not enter the approved Distribution Package.

The design keeps technical detail visible without implying live generation or a publishing connector. **Disclosure:** synthetic data, deterministic output, and no external publishing. Inspect the local reference implementation.

forum.title: How should one governed asset be adapted for different communities?
forum.summary: A discussion prompt about preserving governance while changing editorial form.
forum.body:
A little context: the BBA Publisher Reference Demo starts with governed knowledge, retrieves relevant policies, creates an Institutional Asset, and requires human authorization before preparing distribution variants.

The interesting design question is what happens next. A short social post, a technical article, and a community discussion should not receive the same text. They need different context, tone, structure, and calls to action while preserving the same core claims and source lineage.

This reference package adapts the approved asset per Channel Profile and reviews each variant independently. **Disclosure:** synthetic data, deterministic output, and no external publishing. What would you add to this governed workflow?
